target: chi(G_{n,5}) = 3 a.a.s. via the Diaz-Kaporis-Kemkes-Kirousis-Perez-Wormald Maximum Hypothesis
statement: For the uniformly random simple 5-regular graph G_{n,5}, prove lim_{n->inf, n even} P[chi(G_{n,5}) = 3] = 1, or certify that the published Maximum Hypothesis (the only missing step of the conditional proof) is false.
sufficient_finite_statement: Hypothesis 1.1 of Diaz et al., J. Graph Theory 61 (2009) 157-191: the function F(n_1..n_4) on the stated polytope has a unique global maximum at (1/9,1/9,1/9,1/9). Exact definitions must be re-extracted from the primary text by the worker (scout transcription is a lead only).

primary_attestations.source: Ayre, Coja-Oghlan, Greenhill, arXiv:1812.09691v4 (19 Oct 2021), Section 1.1; Combinatorica 42 (2022)
primary_attestations.quote: Diaz, Kaporis, Kemkes, Kirousis, Perez and Wormald [18] showed that chi(G(n,5)) = 3 w.h.p. if a certain optimisation problem attains its maximum at a specific point, for which they provided numerical evidence.

primary_attestations.source: Diaz et al. 2009 author preprint (Wayback 2021-03-15 snapshot of users.monash.edu.au/~nwormald/papers/3col.pdf), Section 1
primary_attestations.quote: the main outstanding open question on the chromatic number of low-degree random regular graphs ... is the chromatic number of a 5-regular graph a.a.s. 3?
Thus, determining chi(G(n,5)) remains an open problem.

baseline: Proven chi(G_{n,5}) in {3,4} a.a.s. (Shi-Wormald). Conditional chi=3 (Diaz et al. 2009) under the Maximum Hypothesis supported by grid numerics that skipped a 1/1000 boundary layer and relied on numerically confirmed concavity. No 2024-2026 resolution located by the screen or parent web search; EulerSolve OPG-37656 (17 Oct 2026, unrefereed) proves the analogous degree-four second-moment maximum for random lifts of K5, a different model; its techniques may be read and credited.
book_link: Physics volume article p0422 (Alava, Aurell, Zhou; book pp. 422-427): CSPs as spin glasses; Challenge 5 asks for rigorous bounds on SAT/UNSAT transition points. 3-colourability of random 5-regular graphs = zero-temperature 3-state Potts antiferromagnet; related, not verbatim.

acceptance.positive: Outward-rounded interval (or exact) certificate that the maximum is unique at the centre over the FULL domain including boundary layers, with two independent implementations of F/F-hat, plus an audit that the hypothesis as certified is exactly the one used by the conditional proof (Lemmas 5.1-5.10, Section 6, n not 0 mod 6 case). Then hostile cross-vendor review and priority audit.
acceptance.negative: An explicit rational feasible point with certified F-hat > F(centre): refutes the published hypothesis; leaves chi(G_{n,5}) open.

insufficient: Denser grids or multistart numerics alone
Local concavity at the centre alone
Certification of a modified/simplified function without an exact bridge
first_cycle: <=2 h, checkpoint ~60 min: re-derive exact definitions from the primary preprint; reproduce anchors (lambda at centre, F(centre)=5^(5/2)*25/24 per scout, symmetry group); full-domain multistart search including boundary layers; design the rigorous upper-bound scheme (e.g. Lagrangian/dual decomposition into low-dimensional interval subproblems) and test it on a reduced control.
resources: <=4 CPU workers, target <=8 GiB RSS, <=30 min uncheckpointed compute, lane-local venv allowed (e.g. python-flint/arb), downloads <2 GiB.
